newsitem.title: USA: US joins other allies in isolating Bosnia envoy.
newsitem.headline: US joins other allies in isolating Bosnia envoy.

text.p: The United States joined Western European allies on Monday in suspending contact with Bosnian envoys to try to force a fair division of ambassadorial posts.
"We intend to suspend contact with the accredited Bosnian ambassador, effective immediately," State Department spokesman James Foley told reporters.
Foley offered no details of how the suspension would be implemented, but said it would have no effect on economic development assistance to Bosnia.
The U.S. move was in line with actions taken by France, Britain, Sweden and Austria after Germany became the first country to make the move on Sunday.
The international community's high representative in Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, had recommended the action after Bosnian leaders failed to meet an Aug. 1 deadline for agreement on the ambassadors.
Each of the Serb, Moslem and Croat factions in Bosnia wants the plum post at the head of the Washington embassy. The factions have to divide 33 ambassadorial posts among them.
